title: Coefficient-sized inverse image preserves ordinary flat module sheaves
statement: Let f:Y→X be a morphism of schemes and A a commutative ring in Type(max v (u+1)). On the coefficient-sized pro-etale model sites, the fixed-scalar inverse-image functor coefficientProEtaleFixedModulePullback f A [def-sfb-affine-locally-constructible-proetale-modules] preserves flat objects. Here a module sheaf is flat when tensoring on either side is exact; this is the ordinary site-flatness condition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] under the normalized constant-scalar equivalence [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor]. There is no hypothesis on A, f or the module other than flatness of the input.

source.place: Tag 05VD, lemma-pullback-flat; Tag 03CY, constant coefficient ring interpretation.

proof.text: The coefficient-sized base-change functor preserves finite limits and is continuous, hence is representably flat. Apply the constant-scalar algebraic-pullback comparison to obtain an algebraic inverse image with the concrete fixed-scalar inverse-image square.

Given a categorically flat fixed-scalar module M, take its inverse under the normalized scalar equivalence. Its counit identifies the restriction with M, and flat_iff turns the right tensor exactness into ordinary site flatness. Apply the proved algebraic inverse-image flatness theorem to the set-sheaf pullback adjunction, whose inverse image preserves finite limits.

Use flat_iff on the target to get exactness of right tensor. The braiding identifies left tensor with right tensor, giving both components of categorical flatness. Finally transport flatness along the algebraic comparison followed by the fixed-scalar pullback of the source equivalence counit.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05VD, lemma-pullback-flat; Tags 03CY and 03D2; Sites, Proposition 00YV.
proof_origin.note: Lean proof applies the proved universe-polymorphic algebraic flatness theorem and explicitly transports site flatness to both categorical tensor factors. The remaining algebraic identification is isolated in lem-sfb-constant-scalar-algebraic-pullback, without a flatness hypothesis or conclusion. This is a one-hole decomposition, not a net hole closure.
